text:
You need a redesign partner who can turn HeyInternet into a more modern, user-friendly web app and then build the approved design into a responsive, working product.

I’m Tobias Reyne, and I bring 7 years of experience working across full stack web development with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. For your project, I’d approach the work in two clear phases: first, I’d create a high-fidelity mockup that focuses on clarity, usability, and visual polish; then, once the direction is approved, I’d implement the interface into a clean, responsive web application in HTML, CSS, and PHP.

My process starts by understanding the current user flow and the functionality HeyInternet needs to support. From there, I’d translate those requirements into a structured mockup that makes the experience easier to navigate and more visually consistent. I pay close attention to layout, hierarchy, spacing, and responsiveness so the final design feels intentional across devices and browsers. After approval, I’d move into development and make sure the implementation is efficient, maintainable, and aligned with the approved UI.

A relevant project was a restaurant ordering web app for Saffron Lane Kitchens. I built an installable ordering app for 9 restaurants that kept the menu and cart working on bad connections. That project also achieved 22% of orders through the app within 2 months. It required balancing interface clarity with reliable functionality, which is directly relevant to a web app redesign where user experience and smooth execution both matter.

I work well independently, communicate clearly, and keep the scope organized so you know what’s happening at each stage. If helpful, I can also structure the work around milestones for the mockup phase and development phase so feedback stays manageable and progress stays visible.

What parts of HeyInternet’s current interface are most important to preserve, and what are the top 2–3 user pain points you want the redesign to solve first?
